questions.question:
Ravi had _____________ younger brother who taught at _____________ university. He was widely regarded as _____________ honorable man.
Select the option with the correct sequence of articles to fill in the blanks.
questions.explanation:
"Younger brother" and "honorable man" are both non-specific, first-mention nouns (indefinite), so they take the indefinite article "a"/"an" (chosen by the following sound: "a" before a consonant sound in "younger," "an" before the vowel sound in "honorable," since the "h" is silent). "University," despite starting with a vowel letter, starts with a consonant sound ("yoo-niversity"), so it takes "a," not "an."

So the sequence is: a (younger brother), a (university), an (honorable man).

Answer: a; a; an

If p, q, r, s are distinct integers such that:[latex]f(p,q,r,s)= max (p,q,r,s)[/latex]

fg(1, 4, 6, 8) = max [latex]\times[/latex] min = 8 [latex]\times[/latex] 1 = 8

questions.question:
A shop has 4 distinct flavors of ice-cream. One can purchase any number of scoops of any flavor. The order in which the scoops are purchased is inconsequential.  
If one wants to purchase 3 scoops of ice-cream, in how many ways can one make that purchase?
questions.explanation:
We're distributing [latex]3[/latex] identical scoops among [latex]4[/latex] distinct flavors, where any flavor can be chosen any number of times (including zero) and order doesn't matter — a classic stars-and-bars (combinations with repetition) count:

[latex]\binom{n+r-1}{r}=\binom{3+4-1}{3}=\binom63=20[/latex]

Answer: 20

Answer: P = Thirst, Q = Hunger
